Hi Evan + Priya,

Congrats again on signing — excited to get Aurora Labs into staging. Attached is the first-draft MAP Sprint Handbook I promised; it embeds the post-signature implementation plan (rollout phases, canary gates, migration windows, and a train-the-trainer cadence). The goal for this week is to align on acceptance gates and confirm the two-week canary window.

Key asks:
- Please review the high-level rollout phases in the handbook (Section 1) and call out any internal blackout dates by EOD Wednesday.
- Are the two canary cohorts (10% traffic + 60% traffic) acceptable, or do you want a narrower ramp?
- Confirm training participants: we need 3 engineers + 2 ops leads for the train-the-trainer sessions.

Attachments: MAP_Sprint_Handbook_v1.pdf (map + tasks), canary-checklist.xlsx (detailed gate criteria)

Tentative schedule (subject to your blackout dates):
- Week 1 (staging prep): config + integration validation
- Week 2 (canary cohort A): 10% traffic, daily acceptance checks
- Week 3 (canary cohort B): 60% traffic, rollback rehearsal mid-week
- Week 4 (migration + ramp): full cutover window + handback docs

I copied Marissa and Karthik for delivery/engagement ops. If that looks good I can lock in calendar invites and the HubSpot milestones.

Thanks,

--
Soojin Lee

Thanks Soojin — this is helpful. Quick responses inline: 

- Blackout dates: leadership offsite on Jun 6-8; ops on-call rotations Jun 12-13 (we should avoid critical migration tasks those days).
- Canary cohorts: 10% then 50% (we'd prefer 50% for the second cohort rather than 60% to reduce blast radius).
- Training: I can nominate 3 engineers (Sam, Leila, Jose). Ops leads will be Priya + Arvind (I'll confirm Arvind by tomorrow).

A couple of asks from our side: can we add an explicit performance baseline check at the end of canary week A (p99 latency + token throughput)? Also would like the rollback play documented in the handbook (step-by-step).

On the rollback play: draft below (I'll add the exact CLI lines into the workbook later):

1) Isolate failing instances and mark route as drained
2) Reweight traffic to previous model variant (traffic-manager reweight --from variant-b --to variant-a --percent 100)
3) Validate KV cache integrity and warm start previous model if needed
4) Close out incident and run post-mortem checklist

I'll populate the "Rollback" tab in canary-checklist.xlsx with the CLI commands and a short validation script for p99 comparison. Also adding a quick KV cache sanity check (check hit rate > 85% after warmup).
